messages.content: I have a supplier audit in the St. Louis area on Wednesday, January 20 and Thursday, January 21. The opening meeting is at 8:00 Wednesday morning, and the closing meeting should finish by 3:30 Thursday. Please build an approval comparison for traveling Tuesday through Thursday versus staying until Friday morning.
I can compare both schedules. Are you leaving from SFO, and do you have the site location or at least the suburb? The Thursday airport margin will depend heavily on that.

Yes, SFO. The site is in Chesterfield Valley, near the Spirit of St. Louis Airport. Tuesday travel is approved. I need flight times, full trip totals, a practical hotel near the site, and local transportation included.

The most workable Tuesday outbound is United nonstop from SFO at 10:40 a.m., arriving STL at 4:28 p.m. It leaves enough time to collect a rental car and reach Chesterfield before the evening commute fully clears. The current round-trip pairing with a Thursday 6:15 p.m. return is $548 in standard economy. That return reaches SFO at 8:45 p.m.

For Friday, the same outbound paired with United's 8:05 a.m. nonstop from STL is $476, arriving SFO at 10:35 a.m. The lower fare partly offsets the extra hotel night. There are earlier Tuesday departures with connections, but they cost more and do not improve the arrival enough to justify the added risk.
How narrow is the Thursday return in practice? Do not just use the published drive time.

It is quite narrow. If the closing meeting ends exactly at 3:30 p.m., allowing ten minutes to leave the building puts departure near 3:40. The drive from Chesterfield Valley to the rental-car return is commonly 30 to 40 minutes at that hour, but congestion can push it beyond 45. Returning the car and taking the shuttle could add 20 to 30 minutes. That would put you at the terminal around 4:40 to 4:55 for a 6:15 departure, roughly 80 to 95 minutes before takeoff.

It works if the meeting ends on time and traffic is ordinary. A 20-minute overrun or a slow rental return would reduce the margin substantially. I would describe it in the authorization as feasible but operationally exposed, not as a comfortable itinerary.
Check whether there is a later nonstop Thursday. A connection that gets me home after midnight is not useful.

The 6:15 p.m. United flight is the last Thursday nonstop to SFO in the current schedule. The later choices connect through Denver or Dallas and arrive at SFO between 11:48 p.m. and 12:36 a.m. They cost from $521 to $589 and do not offer a good tradeoff. The Friday 8:05 a.m. nonstop is the cleaner alternative.
All right. Compare hotels near the site. I do not need downtown, and I do not want to create a long drive before an 8:00 opening.

Three practical options are available in Chesterfield: the Courtyard St. Louis Chesterfield, about seven minutes from the site, totals $318 for Tuesday and Wednesday nights or $477 through Thursday night; the Drury Plaza Hotel St. Louis Chesterfield, about ten minutes away, totals $344 for two nights or $516 for three; and Hyatt Place St. Louis/Chesterfield, about twelve minutes away, totals $372 for two nights or $558 for three. All three include taxes and free parking.

The Courtyard is the lowest fixed lodging cost and has the shortest site drive, but breakfast is extra. Drury includes breakfast and an evening food service, which may reduce meal expense, though its room total is $26 to $39 higher. Hyatt Place is the most expensive of the three without a meaningful location advantage for this assignment.
Use the Courtyard for the comparison. Is a rental car actually better than rideshare once parking is free?

Yes. A compact rental is currently $186 from Tuesday afternoon through Thursday evening, or $232 through Friday morning. Estimated fuel is $28 for the shorter trip and $32 for the longer one. Hotel parking is free, and the supplier site also has complimentary visitor parking.

Rideshare would likely run $55 to $75 each way between STL and Chesterfield, plus roughly $14 to $22 for each hotel-site trip. With airport transfers and four audit commutes, the expected range is about $166 to $238 before surge pricing or tips. It might narrowly beat the Thursday rental at the low end, but it adds pickup uncertainty on both audit mornings and after the closing meeting. The rental is the more defensible operational choice.

Give me the full totals now, but separate transportation, lodging, and airfare. Include reasonable meals for approval; the company uses $64 per full day, and Tuesday and Friday travel days are capped at 75 percent. Thursday counts as a full day if I fly that evening.

Using the Courtyard and a compact rental, the Tuesday-through-Thursday option is: $548 airfare, $318 lodging, $186 rental car, $28 fuel, and $176 meals. Meals are $48 Tuesday plus $64 Wednesday and $64 Thursday. The authorization total is $1,256.

The Tuesday-through-Friday option is: $476 airfare, $477 lodging, $232 rental car, $32 fuel, and $224 meals. Meals are $48 Tuesday, $64 each for Wednesday and Thursday, and $48 Friday. The authorization total is $1,441.

Staying Friday costs $185 more overall. The extra hotel night, rental day, fuel, and Friday meals add $201, while the airfare drops by $72.
Friday breakfast would be included in the travel-day allowance, but I would leave the hotel too early to buy much. Keep the policy amount anyway. Are there any hotel cancellation or deposit issues?

The Courtyard rates used here are flexible rates. No advance deposit is required, and either reservation can be cancelled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time on Monday, January 18. A late cancellation or no-show would be charged one night plus tax. Payment is due at the hotel. The quoted totals include room tax and free parking but not optional purchases.
Before I choose, show me what happens if the closing meeting goes to 4:00 on Thursday.

A 4:00 p.m. finish would likely mean leaving the site around 4:10. With a 35-to-50-minute drive, rental return, shuttle, and security, you would probably reach the gate area only 35 to 60 minutes before the 6:15 departure. At the slower end, checked baggage would be especially problematic because the carrier cutoff could already be near or passed. Even with carry-on only, the plan would have little recovery time for traffic or a rental shuttle delay.

For approval purposes, the Thursday itinerary should be conditioned on a firm 3:30 adjournment and immediate departure. If the meeting may run to 4:00, the Friday flight is the credible plan.
There will be audit records to bring back, so assume I check a bag. Does the airfare include that?

No. The quoted standard economy fares do not include a checked bag. Adding one bag each way is estimated at $80 round trip, making airfare $628 for the Thursday return or $556 for the Friday return. The revised trip totals are therefore $1,336 for Tuesday through Thursday and $1,521 for Tuesday through Friday. The cost difference remains $185.
That settles it. Prepare the authorization around the Friday return. Mention the Thursday option as rejected because the timing is not reliable with a checked bag. Do not book anything yet.

Authorization-ready plan: travel Tuesday, January 19 through Friday, January 22 for the two-day supplier audit in Chesterfield Valley. Fly United nonstop SFO-STL Tuesday from 10:40 a.m. to 4:28 p.m., then return nonstop Friday from 8:05 a.m. to 10:35 a.m. Standard economy plus one checked bag is estimated at $556.

Lodging is the Courtyard St. Louis Chesterfield for three nights at $477 including tax, with free parking and a drive of about seven minutes to the site. The flexible rate requires no deposit and is cancellable until 6:00 p.m. local time January 18. A compact rental car is estimated at $232, with $32 for fuel. Meal allowance is $224.

The total requested authorization is $1,521: $556 airfare, $477 lodging, $264 local transportation, and $224 meals. The Tuesday-through-Thursday alternative was evaluated at $1,336 but rejected because a 3:30 p.m. closing leaves limited tolerance for traffic, rental return, security, and checked-bag deadlines before the last 6:15 p.m. nonstop. No flight, hotel, or car has been booked.
